title: एकोनत्रिंशदधिकत्रिशततमोऽध्यायः

summary.en: Arjuna asks Krishna how Fire and Soma were first made of one womb, and Krishna tells how the three-headed Vishvarupa, the gods' priest and nephew of the asuras, gave the gods their share openly and the asuras theirs in secret. Indra slew him, and Tvashtri made Vritra to avenge him.
summary.kn: ಅಗ್ನಿ-ಸೋಮ ಹೇಗೆ ಒಂದೇ ಯೋನಿಯಿಂದ ಮೊದಲು ಹುಟ್ಟಿದವೆಂದು ಅರ್ಜುನ ಕೃಷ್ಣನನ್ನು ಕೇಳುತ್ತಾನೆ; ದೇವತೆಗಳ ಪುರೋಹಿತ, ಅಸುರರ ಸೋದರಳಿಯ ತ್ರಿಶಿರ ವಿಶ್ವರೂಪ ದೇವತೆಗಳಿಗೆ ಬಹಿರಂಗ, ಅಸುರರಿಗೆ ರಹಸ್ಯ ಭಾಗ ಕೊಟ್ಟನೆಂದು ಕೃಷ್ಣ ಹೇಳುತ್ತಾನೆ. ಇಂದ್ರ ಅವನನ್ನು ಕೊಂದ, ತ್ವಷ್ಟೃ ಪ್ರತೀಕಾರಕ್ಕೆ ವೃತ್ರನನ್ನು ಸೃಷ್ಟಿಸಿದ.
summary.hi: अर्जुन कृष्ण से पूछते हैं कि अग्नि और सोम पहले एक योनि से कैसे बने, और कृष्ण बताते हैं कि देवताओं के पुरोहित और असुरों के भानजे त्रिशिर विश्वरूप ने देवताओं को खुला और असुरों को छिपा भाग दिया। इन्द्र ने उसे मारा और त्वष्टा ने बदले के लिए वृत्र रचा।
summary.te: అగ్ని, సోమం ఒకే యోని నుండి మొదట ఎలా ఏర్పడ్డాయని అర్జునుడు కృష్ణుని అడుగుతాడు; దేవతల పురోహితుడు, అసురుల మేనల్లుడు త్రిశిరుడు విశ్వరూపుడు దేవతలకు బహిరంగంగా, అసురులకు రహస్యంగా భాగం ఇచ్చాడని కృష్ణుడు చెబుతాడు. ఇంద్రుడు అతన్ని చంపగా త్వష్ట ప్రతీకారానికి వృత్రుని సృష్టించాడు.
summary.ta: அக்னியும் சோமனும் ஒரே கருவில் எவ்வாறு முதலில் உருவாயின என்று அர்ஜுனன் கண்ணனைக் கேட்க, தேவரின் புரோகிதனும் அசுரரின் மருமகனுமான மூன்று தலை விசுவரூபன் தேவருக்கு வெளிப்படையாகவும் அசுரருக்கு ரகசியமாகவும் பங்கு தந்ததைக் கண்ணன் கூறுகிறான். இந்திரன் அவனைக் கொல்ல, துவஷ்டா பழிவாங்க வித்ரனைப் படைத்தான்.
summary.ml: അഗ്നിയും സോമനും ആദ്യം ഒരേ ഗർഭത്തിൽനിന്ന് ഉണ്ടായതെങ്ങനെയെന്ന് അർജുനൻ കൃഷ്ണനോട് ചോദിക്കുന്നു; മൂന്നു തലയുള്ള വിശ്വരൂപൻ, ദേവന്മാരുടെ പുരോഹിതനും അസുരന്മാരുടെ മരുമകനുമായിരുന്നു, അദ്ദേഹം ദേവന്മാർക്ക് അവരുടെ പങ്ക് പരസ്യമായും അസുരന്മാർക്ക് രഹസ്യമായും നൽകിയതെങ്ങനെയെന്ന് കൃഷ്ണൻ പറയുന്നു. ഇന്ദ്രൻ അദ്ദേഹത്തെ വധിച്ചു, അതിന് പകരം ചോദിക്കാൻ ത്വഷ്ടാവ് വൃത്രനെ സൃഷ്ടിച്ചു.

source: Mahabharata, Critical Edition (BORI, Pune) 12.329; e-text by M. Tokunaga and J. D. Smith, © BORI 1999, version of Wed Jun 16 2021

verses.text: अर्जुन उवाच

meaning.en: Arjuna said:

verses.text:
अग्नीषोमौ कथं पूर्वमेकयोनी प्रवर्तितौ ।
एष मे संशयो जातस्तं छिन्धि मधुसूदन ॥

meaning.en: How were Agni and Soma first made to share one womb? This doubt has arisen in me; resolve it, Madhusudana.

verses.text: श्रीभगवानुवाच

meaning.en: The Blessed Lord said:

verses.text:
हन्त ते वर्तयिष्यामि पुराणं पाण्डुनन्दन ।
आत्मतेजोद्भवं पार्थ शृणुष्वैकमना मम ॥

meaning.en: Gladly, son of Pandu, I will tell you the ancient account, born of my own radiance. Listen to me with a single mind.

verses.text:
संप्रक्षालनकालेऽतिक्रान्ते चतुर्थे युगसहस्रान्ते ।
अव्यक्ते सर्वभूतप्रलये स्थावरजङ्गमे ।
ज्योतिर्धरणिवायुरहितेऽन्धे तमसि जलैकार्णवे लोके ।
तम इत्येवाभिभूतेऽसंज्ञकेऽद्वितीये प्रतिष्ठिते ।
नैव रात्र्यां न दिवसे न सति नासति न व्यक्ते नाव्यक्ते व्यवस्थिते ।
एतस्यामवस्थायां नारायणगुणाश्रयादक्षयादजरादनिन्द्रियादग्राह्यादसंभवात्सत्यादहिंस्राल्ललामाद्विविधप्रवृत्तिविशेषात् ।
अक्षयादजरामरादमूर्तितः सर्वव्यापिनः सर्वकर्तुः शाश्वतात्तमसः पुरुषः प्रादुर्भूतो हरिरव्ययः ॥

meaning.en: After the time of dissolution had passed, at the end of the fourth thousand-yuga cycle, when all beings, moving and unmoving, had dissolved into the unmanifest, the world was one ocean of water in blind darkness, without light, earth, or wind, overwhelmed by darkness, nameless and without a second; it was neither night nor day, neither being nor non-being, neither manifest nor unmanifest. In that state, from the imperishable, ageless, senseless, ungraspable, unborn, true, harmless, auspicious Narayana, of manifold activity and without form, all-pervading maker of all, from the eternal darkness, the Person Hari, the imperishable, appeared.

verses.text:
निदर्शनमपि ह्यत्र भवति ।
नासीदहो न रात्रिरासीत् ।
न सदासीन्नासदासीत् ।
तम एव पुरस्तादभवद्विश्वरूपम् ।
सा विश्वस्य जननीत्येवमस्यार्थोऽनुभाष्यते ॥

meaning.en: There is a testimony here too: "There was no day, there was no night; neither being nor non-being; darkness alone lay first, of every form, the mother of the universe." This is how the text's meaning is echoed.

verses.text:
तस्येदानीं तमःसंभवस्य पुरुषस्य पद्मयोनेर्ब्रह्मणः प्रादुर्भावे स पुरुषः प्रजाः सिसृक्षमाणो नेत्राभ्यामग्नीषोमौ ससर्ज ।
ततो भूतसर्गे प्रवृत्ते प्रजाक्रमवशाद्ब्रह्मक्षत्रमुपातिष्ठत् ।
यः सोमस्तद्ब्रह्म यद्ब्रह्म ते ब्राह्मणाः ।
योऽग्निस्तत्क्षत्रं क्षत्राद्ब्रह्म बलवत्तरम् ।
कस्मादिति लोकप्रत्यक्षगुणमेतत्तद्यथा ।
ब्राह्मणेभ्यः परं भूतं नोत्पन्नपूर्वम् ।
दीप्यमानेऽग्नौ जुहोतीति कृत्वा ब्रवीमि ।
भूतसर्गः कृतो ब्रह्मणा भूतानि च प्रतिष्ठाप्य त्रैलोक्यं धार्यत इति ॥

meaning.en: Now when Brahma, the lotus-born Person arising from that darkness, appeared, the Person, wishing to create beings, made Agni and Soma from his eyes. Then, as creation proceeded, in the order of beings, the brahmin and the kshatriya arose. Soma is the brahmin power, and those are the brahmins; Agni is the kshatriya power; and the brahmin is stronger than the kshatriya. Why? This quality is plain to the world: nothing higher than brahmins has ever been born before, and one offers into a blazing fire. Brahma made the creation of beings and, establishing them, sustains the three worlds.

verses.text:
मन्त्रवादोऽपि हि भवति ।
त्वमग्ने यज्ञानां होता विश्वेषाम् ।
हितो देवेभिर्मानुषे जने इति ।
निदर्शनं चात्र भवति ।
विश्वेषामग्ने यज्ञानां होतेति ।
हितो देवैर्मानुषैर्जगत इति ।
अग्निर्हि यज्ञानां होता कर्ता ।
स चाग्निर्ब्रह्म ॥

meaning.en: There is also a Vedic verse: "You, Agni, are the priest of all the sacrifices, placed by the gods among the human people." A commentary on it says Agni is the priest and doer of sacrifices, and that Agni is Brahman.

verses.text:
न ह्यृते मन्त्राद्धवनमस्ति ।
न विना पुरुषं तपः संभवति ।
हविर्मन्त्राणां संपूजा विद्यते देवमनुष्याणामनेन त्वं होतेति नियुक्तः ।
ये च मानुषा होत्राधिकारास्ते च ।
ब्राह्मणस्य हि याजनं विधीयते न क्षत्रवैश्ययोर्द्विजात्योः ।
तस्माद्ब्राह्मणा ह्यग्निभूता यज्ञानुद्वहन्ति ।
यज्ञा देवांस्तर्पयन्ति देवाः पृथिवीं भावयन्ति ॥

meaning.en: For there is no offering without mantra, and no austerity without a person. The oblation and mantras are honored by gods and men, and by them you were appointed priest; and the human offices of priest belong to him too. Officiating at sacrifices is prescribed for the brahmin, not for the kshatriya or vaishya. So brahmins, being Agni, carry the sacrifices; sacrifices satisfy the gods, and the gods nourish the earth.

verses.text:
शतपथे हि ब्राह्मणं भवति ।
अग्नौ समिद्धे स जुहोति यो विद्वान्ब्राह्मणमुखे दानाहुतिं जुहोति ।
एवमप्यग्निभूता ब्राह्मणा विद्वांसोऽग्निं भावयन्ति ।
अग्निर्विष्णुः सर्वभूतान्यनुप्रविश्य प्राणान्धारयति ।
अपि चात्र सनत्कुमारगीताः श्लोका भवन्ति ॥

meaning.en: The Shatapatha Brahmana says that one offers into the kindled fire who, being learned, offers a gift into a brahmin's mouth. So the learned brahmins, who are Agni, nourish Agni. Agni is Vishnu, entering all beings and sustaining their breaths. Here are also verses sung by Sanatkumara.

verses.text:
विश्वं ब्रह्मासृजत्पूर्वं सर्वादिर्निरवस्करम् ।
ब्रह्मघोषैर्दिवं तिष्ठन्त्यमरा ब्रह्मयोनयः ॥

meaning.en: Brahma first created the universe, the origin of all, complete without remainder; the immortals, born of Brahman, dwell in heaven through the chanting of Brahman.

verses.text:
ब्राह्मणानां मतिर्वाक्यं कर्म श्रद्धा तपांसि च ।
धारयन्ति महीं द्यां च शैत्याद्वार्यमृतं यथा ॥

meaning.en: The brahmins' thought, speech, rites, faith, and austerities uphold the earth and sky, as coolness holds back the nectar.

verses.text:
नास्ति सत्यात्परो धर्मो नास्ति मातृसमो गुरुः ।
ब्राह्मणेभ्यः परं नास्ति प्रेत्य चेह च भूतये ॥

meaning.en: There is no dharma higher than truth, no teacher equal to a mother, and nothing higher than brahmins for welfare here and hereafter.

verses.text:
नैषामुक्षा वर्धते नोत वाहा
न गर्गरो मथ्यते संप्रदाने ।
अपध्वस्ता दस्युभूता भवन्ति
येषां राष्ट्रे ब्राह्मणा वृत्तिहीनाः ॥

meaning.en: Their bull does not grow, nor their cart-ox, and the churn is not turned at the giving; they become ruined and like bandits, in whose kingdom brahmins lack a livelihood.

verses.text:
वेदपुराणेतिहासप्रामाण्यान्नारायणमुखोद्गताः सर्वात्मानः सर्वकर्तारः सर्वभावनाश्च ब्राह्मणाः ।
वाक्समकालं हि तस्य देवस्य वरप्रदस्य ब्राह्मणाः प्रथमं प्रादुर्भूता ब्राह्मणेभ्यश्च शेषा वर्णाः प्रादुर्भूताः ।
इत्थं च सुरासुरविशिष्टा ब्राह्मणा यदा मया ब्रह्मभूतेन पुरा स्वयमेवोत्पादिताः सुरासुरमहर्षयो भूतविशेषाः स्थापिता निगृहीताश्च ॥

meaning.en: By the authority of Veda, Purana, and Itihasa, brahmins issued from Narayana's mouth, are the self of all, makers of all, and nourishers of all. At the same moment as the word of that boon-giving god, brahmins appeared first, and from brahmins the other classes. So brahmins, eminent among gods and asuras, were produced by me myself, having become Brahman; and gods, asuras, great sages, and other beings were established and restrained.

verses.text:
अहल्याधर्षणनिमित्तं हि गौतमाद्धरिश्मश्रुतामिन्द्रः प्राप्तः ।
कौशिकनिमित्तं चेन्द्रो मुष्कवियोगं मेषवृषणत्वं चावाप ।
अश्विनोर्ग्रहप्रतिषेधोद्यतवज्रस्य पुरंदरस्य च्यवनेन स्तम्भितो बाहुः ।
क्रतुवधप्राप्तमन्युना च दक्षेण भूयस्तपसा चात्मानं संयोज्य नेत्राकृतिरन्या ललाटे रुद्रस्योत्पादिता ॥

meaning.en: For molesting Ahalya, Indra got from Gautama a beard of tawny hair. Because of Kaushika, Indra lost his testicles and gained a ram's. When Purandara raised his thunderbolt to forbid the Ashvins' soma cup, Chyavana paralyzed his arm. And Daksha, angry at the destruction of his rite, united himself with great austerity and produced another eye-shaped mark on Rudra's forehead.

verses.text:
त्रिपुरवधार्थं दीक्षामभ्युपगतस्य रुद्रस्योशनसा शिरसो जटा उत्कृत्य प्रयुक्ताः ।
ततः प्रादुर्भूता भुजगाः ।
तैरस्य भुजगैः पीड्यमानः कण्ठो नीलतामुपनीतः ।
पूर्वे च मन्वन्तरे स्वायंभुवे नारायणहस्तबन्धग्रहणान्नीलकण्ठत्वमेव वा ॥

meaning.en: When Rudra undertook the initiation to slay the Tripuras, Ushanas tore out locks from his head and hurled them; snakes arose from them, and tormented by those snakes his throat was turned blue; or alternatively, in the earlier Svayambhuva Manu era, his blue throat came from Narayana's grasp of his hand.

verses.text:
अमृतोत्पादने पुरश्चरणतामुपगतस्याङ्गिरसो बृहस्पतेरुपस्पृशतो न प्रसादं गतवत्यः किलापः ।
अथ बृहस्पतिरपां चुक्रोध ।
यस्मान्ममोपस्पृशतः कलुषीभूता न प्रसादमुपगतास्तस्मादद्यप्रभृति झषमकरमत्स्यकच्छपजन्तुसंकीर्णाः कलुषीभवतेति ।
तदाप्रभृत्यापो यादोभिः संकीर्णाः संवृत्ताः ॥

meaning.en: At the churning for nectar, when Brihaspati Angirasa, acting as the forerunner, touched the waters, they did not become clear. Brihaspati grew angry at the waters: "Since you grew muddy when I touched you, from today you will be muddy, filled with fish, crocodiles, tortoises, and creatures." Since then the waters have been crowded with aquatic animals.

verses.text:
विश्वरूपो वै त्वाष्ट्रः पुरोहितो देवानामासीत्स्वस्रीयोऽसुराणाम् ।
स प्रत्यक्षं देवेभ्यो भागमददत्परोक्षमसुरेभ्यः ॥

meaning.en: Vishvarupa, son of Tvashtri, was the gods' priest and the asuras' sister's son. He gave the gods their share openly and the asuras theirs secretly.

verses.text:
अथ हिरण्यकशिपुं पुरस्कृत्य विश्वरूपमातरं स्वसारमसुरा वरमयाचन्त ।
हे स्वसरयं ते पुत्रस्त्वाष्ट्रो विश्वरूपस्त्रिशिरा देवानां पुरोहितः प्रत्यक्षं देवेभ्यो भागमददत्परोक्षमस्माकम् ।
ततो देवा वर्धन्ते वयं क्षीयामः ।
तदेनं त्वं वारयितुमर्हसि तथा यथास्मान्भजेदिति ॥

meaning.en: Then the asuras put Hiranyakashipu forward and begged a boon from Vishvarupa's mother, his sister: "Sister, your son Vishvarupa, the three-headed son of Tvashtri, priest of the gods, gives the gods their share openly and ours secretly. So the gods prosper and we decline. You should restrain him so that he will favor us."

verses.text:
अथ विश्वरूपं नन्दनवनमुपगतं मातोवाच ।
पुत्र किं परपक्षवर्धनस्त्वं मातुलपक्षं नाशयसि ।
नार्हस्येवं कर्तुमिति ।
स विश्वरूपो मातुर्वाक्यमनतिक्रमणीयमिति मत्वा संपूज्य हिरण्यकशिपुमगात् ॥

meaning.en: His mother then spoke to Vishvarupa, who had gone to the Nandana grove: "Son, why do you strengthen the enemy's side and destroy your mother's kin? You should not act so." Thinking his mother's word could not be disobeyed, Vishvarupa honored her and went to Hiranyakashipu.

verses.text:
हैरण्यगर्भाच्च वसिष्ठाद्धिरण्यकशिपुः शापं प्राप्तवान् ।
यस्मात्त्वयान्यो वृतो होता तस्मादसमाप्तयज्ञस्त्वमपूर्वात्सत्त्वजाताद्वधं प्राप्स्यसीति ।
तच्छापदानाद्धिरण्यकशिपुः प्राप्तवान्वधम् ॥

meaning.en: Hiranyakashipu received a curse from Vasishtha, born of Hiranyagarbha: "Since you chose another priest, your sacrifice will be unfinished, and you will be killed by a being never before born." Through that curse Hiranyakashipu met his death.

verses.text:
विश्वरूपो मातृपक्षवर्धनोऽत्यर्थं तपस्यभवत् ।
तस्य व्रतभङ्गार्थमिन्द्रो बह्वीः श्रीमत्योऽप्सरसो नियुयोज ।
ताश्च दृष्ट्वा मनः क्षुभितं तस्याभवत्तासु चाप्सरःसु नचिरादेव सक्तोऽभवत् ।
सक्तं चैनं ज्ञात्वाप्सरस ऊचुर्गच्छामहे वयं यथागतमिति ॥

meaning.en: Vishvarupa, favoring his mother's side, practiced extreme austerity. To break his vow, Indra sent many beautiful apsarases. Seeing them, his mind was stirred, and he soon became attached to those apsarases. Knowing he was attached, the apsarases said, "We will go back as we came."

verses.text:
तास्त्वाष्ट्र उवाच ।
क्व गमिष्यथ आस्यतां तावन्मया सह श्रेयो भविष्यतीति ।
तास्तमब्रुवन् ।
वयं देवस्त्रियोऽप्सरस इन्द्रं वरदं पुरा प्रभविष्णुं वृणीमह इति ॥

meaning.en: Tvashtri's son said to them, "Where will you go? Stay with me a while; it will be well for you." They answered, "We are the wives of the gods, apsarases; we choose Indra, the powerful boon-giver, long ago."

verses.text:
अथ ता विश्वरूपोऽब्रवीदद्यैव सेन्द्रा देवा न भविष्यन्तीति ।
ततो मन्त्राञ्जजाप ।
तैर्मन्त्रैः प्रावर्धत त्रिशिराः ।
एकेनास्येन सर्वलोकेषु द्विजैः क्रियावद्भिर्यज्ञेषु सुहुतं सोमं पपावेकेनाप एकेन सेन्द्रान्देवान् ।
अथेन्द्रस्तं विवर्धमानं सोमपानाप्यायितसर्वगात्रं दृष्ट्वा चिन्तामापेदे ॥

meaning.en: Then Vishvarupa said to them, "Today the gods will be without Indra." He recited mantras, and by them the three-headed one grew. With one mouth he drank the soma well offered in sacrifices by rites-performing brahmins in all the worlds, with one he drank water, and with one he drank up the gods with Indra. Seeing him growing, all his limbs swollen with the soma he drank, Indra fell into anxiety.

verses.text:
देवाश्च ते सहेन्द्रेण ब्रह्माणमभिजग्मुरूचुश्च ।
विश्वरूपेण सर्वयज्ञेषु सुहुतः सोमः पीयते ।
वयमभागाः संवृत्ताः ।
असुरपक्षो वर्धते वयं क्षीयामः ।
तदर्हसि नो विधातुं श्रेयो यदनन्तरमिति ॥

meaning.en: The gods with Indra went to Brahma and said, "Vishvarupa drinks the soma well offered at all the sacrifices. We have been left without a share. The asura side grows and we decline. You should decide what is best next."

verses.text:
तान्ब्रह्मोवाच ऋषिर्भार्गवस्तपस्तप्यते दधीचः ।
स याच्यतां वरं यथा कलेवरं जह्यात् ।
तस्यास्थिभिर्वज्रं क्रियतामिति ॥

meaning.en: Brahma said to them, "The Bhargava sage Dadhicha is practicing austerity. Ask him for a boon, that he give up his body, and let a thunderbolt be made from his bones."

verses.text:
देवास्तत्रागच्छन्यत्र दधीचो भगवानृषिस्तपस्तेपे ।
सेन्द्रा देवास्तमभिगम्योचुर्भगवंस्तपसः कुशलमविघ्नं चेति ।
तान्दधीच उवाच स्वागतं भवद्भ्यः किं क्रियताम् ।
यद्वक्ष्यथ तत्करिष्यामीति ।
ते तमब्रुवञ्शरीरपरित्यागं लोकहितार्थं भगवान्कर्तुमर्हतीति ।
अथ दधीचस्तथैवाविमनाः सुखदुःखसमो महायोगी आत्मानं समाधाय शरीरपरित्यागं चकार ॥

meaning.en: The gods went to where the blessed sage Dadhicha was practicing austerity. The gods with Indra approached and said, "Blessed one, is your austerity going well and unhindered?" Dadhicha said to them, "Welcome. What shall be done? I will do whatever you say." They told him, "The blessed one should give up his body for the good of the worlds." Then Dadhicha, equable in pleasure and pain, a great yogi, with an undisturbed mind, composed himself and gave up his body.

verses.text:
तस्य परमात्मन्यवसृते तान्यस्थीनि धाता संगृह्य वज्रमकरोत् ।
तेन वज्रेणाभेद्येनाप्रधृष्येण ब्रह्मास्थिसंभूतेन विष्णुप्रविष्टेनेन्द्रो विश्वरूपं जघान ।
शिरसां चास्य छेदनमकरोत् ।
तस्मादनन्तरं विश्वरूपगात्रमथनसंभवं त्वष्ट्रोत्पादितमेवारिं वृत्रमिन्द्रो जघान ॥

meaning.en: When he had gone into the Supreme Self, Dhatri collected those bones and made a thunderbolt. With that unbreakable, unassailable thunderbolt, made of a brahmin's bones and entered by Vishnu, Indra slew Vishvarupa and cut off his heads. Afterwards Indra slew Vritra, the enemy Tvashtri had produced from the churning of Vishvarupa's body.

verses.text:
तस्यां द्वैधीभूतायां ब्रह्मवध्यायां भयादिन्द्रो देवराज्यं परित्यज्य अप्सु संभवां शीतलां मानससरोगतां नलिनीं प्रपेदे ।
तत्र चैश्वर्ययोगादणुमात्रो भूत्वा बिसग्रन्थिं प्रविवेश ॥

meaning.en: When the brahmin-killing sin split in two, Indra, in fear, abandoned the kingship of the gods and entered a cool lotus-bearing lake in the mind, born of the waters. There, by his lordly power, he became tiny and entered a lotus stalk's fiber.

verses.text:
अथ ब्रह्मवध्याभयप्रनष्टे त्रैलोक्यनाथे शचीपतौ जगदनीश्वरं बभूव ।
देवान्रजस्तमश्चाविवेश ।
मन्त्रा न प्रावर्तन्त महर्षीणाम् ।
रक्षांसि प्रादुरभवन् ।
ब्रह्म चोत्सादनं जगाम ।
अनिन्द्राश्चाबला लोकाः सुप्रधृष्या बभूवुः ॥

meaning.en: When Shachi's lord, master of the three worlds, vanished in fear of the brahmin-killing, the world was left without a lord. Passion and darkness entered the gods, the sages' mantras did not work, demons appeared, sacred knowledge was ruined, and the worlds without Indra became weak and easily assailed.

verses.text:
अथ देवा ऋषयश्चायुषः पुत्रं नहुषं नाम देवराजत्वेऽभिषिषिचुः ।
नहुषः पञ्चभिः शतैर्ज्योतिषां ललाटे ज्वलद्भिः सर्वतेजोहरैस्त्रिविष्टपं पालयां बभूव ।
अथ लोकाः प्रकृतिमापेदिरे स्वस्थाश्च बभूवुः ॥

meaning.en: Then the gods and sages anointed Nahusha, son of Ayu, as king of the gods. With five hundred blazing lights on his forehead, which robbed all others of splendor, Nahusha ruled the heavens. Then the worlds returned to their natural state and were at ease.

verses.text:
अथोवाच नहुषः ।
सर्वं मां शक्रोपभुक्तमुपस्थितमृते शचीमिति ।
स एवमुक्त्वा शचीसमीपमगमदुवाच चैनाम् ।
सुभगेऽहमिन्द्रो देवानां भजस्व मामिति ।
तं शची प्रत्युवाच ।
प्रकृत्या त्वं धर्मवत्सलः सोमवंशोद्भवश्च ।
नार्हसि परपत्नीधर्षणं कर्तुमिति ॥

meaning.en: Nahusha then said, "Everything Shakra enjoyed is now mine, except Shachi." So saying, he went to Shachi and said to her, "Fair one, I am Indra of the gods; accept me." Shachi replied, "By nature you are devoted to dharma and born in the lunar line; you should not assault another's wife."

verses.text:
तामथोवाच नहुषः ।
ऐन्द्रं पदमध्यास्यते मया ।
अहमिन्द्रस्य राज्यरत्नहरो नात्राधर्मः कश्चित्त्वमिन्द्रभुक्तेति ।
सा तमुवाच ।
अस्ति मम किंचिद्व्रतमपर्यवसितम् ।
तस्यावभृथे त्वामुपगमिष्यामि कैश्चिदेवाहोभिरिति ।
स शच्यैवमभिहितो नहुषो जगाम ॥

meaning.en: Nahusha said to her, "I occupy Indra's position; I have taken Indra's kingdom and its jewels, and there is no wrong here; you were Indra's." She said, "I have a vow not yet complete. After its concluding bath I will come to you, in some days." Told this by Shachi, Nahusha left.

verses.text:
अथ शची दुःखशोकार्ता भर्तृदर्शनलालसा नहुषभयगृहीता बृहस्पतिमुपागच्छत् ।
स च तामभिगतां दृष्ट्वैव ध्यानं प्रविश्य भर्तृकार्यतत्परां ज्ञात्वा बृहस्पतिरुवाच ।
अनेनैव व्रतेन तपसा चान्विता देवीं वरदामुपश्रुतिमाह्वय ।
सा तवेन्द्रं दर्शयिष्यतीति ॥

meaning.en: Then Shachi, afflicted with grief and sorrow, longing to see her husband and seized by fear of Nahusha, went to Brihaspati. Seeing her come, he entered meditation and, understanding she was intent on her husband's cause, said, "With this very vow and austerity, invoke the boon-giving goddess Upashruti. She will show you Indra."

verses.text:
साथ महानियममास्थिता देवीं वरदामुपश्रुतिं मन्त्रैराह्वयत् ।
सोपश्रुतिः शचीसमीपमगात् ।
उवाच चैनामियमस्मि त्वयोपहूतोपस्थिता ।
किं ते प्रियं करवाणीति ।
तां मूर्ध्ना प्रणम्योवाच शची भगवत्यर्हसि मे भर्तारं दर्शयितुं त्वं सत्या मता चेति ।
सैनां मानसं सरोऽनयत् ।
तत्रेन्द्रं बिसग्रन्थिगतमदर्शयत् ॥

meaning.en: Then, observing a great vow, she called the boon-giving goddess Upashruti with mantras. Upashruti came to Shachi and said, "Here I am, summoned by you. What pleasing thing shall I do?" Shachi bowed her head and said, "Blessed one, you should show me my husband; you are held to be true." Upashruti led her to the lake in the mind, and there showed her Indra inside the lotus fiber.

verses.text:
तामिन्द्रः पत्नीं कृशां ग्लानां च दृष्ट्वा चिन्तयां बभूव ।
अहो मम महद्दुःखमिदमद्योपगतम् ।
नष्टं हि मामियमन्विष्योपागमद्दुःखार्तेति ।
तामिन्द्र उवाच कथं वर्तयसीति ।
सा तमुवाच ।
नहुषो मामाह्वयति ।
कालश्चास्य मया कृत इति ॥

meaning.en: Seeing his wife thin and weary, Indra was troubled: "Alas, a great sorrow has come to me today; she has searched me out in my disappearance, tormented by grief." Indra asked her, "How are you managing?" She said, "Nahusha is summoning me, and I have set him a time."

verses.text:
तामिन्द्र उवाच ।
गच्छ ।
नहुषस्त्वया वाच्योऽपूर्वेण मामृषियुक्तेन यानेन त्वमधिरूढ उद्वहस्व ।
इन्द्रस्य हि महान्ति वाहनानि मनसः प्रियाण्यधिरूढानि मया ।
त्वमन्येनोपयातुमर्हसीति ।
सैवमुक्ता हृष्टा जगाम ।
इन्द्रोऽपि बिसग्रन्थिमेवाविवेश भूयः ॥

meaning.en: Indra said to her, "Go. Tell Nahusha: 'Come to me riding a new vehicle drawn by sages. Indra's great mounts are ones I have ridden, to my liking; you ought to come by another.'" Told this, she went away glad, and Indra entered the lotus fiber again.

verses.text:
अथेन्द्राणीमभ्यागतां दृष्ट्वोवाच नहुषः पूर्णः स काल इति ।
तं शच्यब्रवीच्छक्रेण यथोक्तम् ।
स महर्षियुक्तं वाहनमधिरूढः शचीसमीपमुपागच्छत् ॥

meaning.en: Seeing Indrani come, Nahusha said, "The time is fulfilled." Shachi told him what Shakra had said. He mounted a conveyance yoked to great sages and came toward Shachi.

verses.text:
अथ मैत्रावरुणिः कुम्भयोनिरगस्त्यो महर्षीन्विक्रियमाणांस्तान्नहुषेणापश्यत् ।
पद्भ्यां च तेनास्पृश्यत ।
ततः स नहुषमब्रवीदकार्यप्रवृत्त पाप पतस्व महीम् ।
सर्पो भव यावद्भूमिर्गिरयश्च तिष्ठेयुस्तावदिति ।
स महर्षिवाक्यसमकालमेव तस्माद्यानादवापतत् ॥

meaning.en: Then Agastya, Maitravaruni, the pot-born, saw those great sages being driven about by Nahusha, and was touched by Nahusha's foot. He said to Nahusha, "Wretch, set on a wrongful act, fall to earth! Become a serpent for as long as earth and mountains endure." At the sage's word he fell from that vehicle.

verses.text:
अथानिन्द्रं पुनस्त्रैलोक्यमभवत् ।
ततो देवा ऋषयश्च भगवन्तं विष्णुं शरणमिन्द्रार्थेऽभिजग्मुः ।
ऊचुश्चैनं भगवन्निन्द्रं ब्रह्मवध्याभिभूतं त्रातुमर्हसीति ।
ततः स वरदस्तानब्रवीदश्वमेधं यज्ञं वैष्णवं शक्रोऽभियजतु ।
ततः स्वं स्थानं प्राप्स्यतीति ॥

meaning.en: Then the three worlds were again without an Indra. The gods and sages went for refuge to the blessed Vishnu for Indra's sake and said, "Blessed one, you should save Indra, overcome by the brahmin-killing." The boon-giver said, "Let Shakra perform the Vaishnava horse sacrifice; then he will regain his place."

verses.text:
ततो देवा ऋषयश्चेन्द्रं नापश्यन्यदा तदा शचीमूचुर्गच्छ सुभगे इन्द्रमानयस्वेति ।
सा पुनस्तत्सरः समभ्यगच्छत् ।
इन्द्रश्च तस्मात्सरसः समुत्थाय बृहस्पतिमभिजगाम ।
बृहस्पतिश्चाश्वमेधं महाक्रतुं शक्रायाहरत् ।
ततः कृष्णसारङ्गं मेध्यमश्वमुत्सृज्य वाहनं तमेव कृत्वा इन्द्रं मरुत्पतिं बृहस्पतिः स्वस्थानं प्रापयामास ॥

meaning.en: Since the gods and sages could not find Indra, they told Shachi, "Go, fair one, and bring Indra." She went again to that lake, and Indra rose from it and went to Brihaspati. Brihaspati brought the great Ashvamedha rite for Shakra. Releasing a black-spotted sacrificial horse and making it his mount, Brihaspati restored Indra, lord of the Maruts, to his place.

verses.text:
ततः स देवराड्देवैरृषिभिः स्तूयमानस्त्रिविष्टपस्थो निष्कल्मषो बभूव ।
ब्रह्मवध्यां चतुर्षु स्थानेषु वनिताग्निवनस्पतिगोषु व्यभजत् ।
एवमिन्द्रो ब्रह्मतेजःप्रभावोपबृंहितः शत्रुवधं कृत्वा स्वस्थानं प्रापितः ॥

meaning.en: Praised by the gods and sages, the king of gods stood in heaven, free of stain. He divided the brahmin-killing sin among four places: women, fire, trees, and cows. Thus Indra, strengthened by the power of brahmins, slew his foe and was restored to his place.

verses.text:
आकाशगङ्गागतश्च पुरा भरद्वाजो महर्षिरुपास्पृशंस्त्रीन्क्रमान्क्रमता विष्णुनाभ्यासादितः ।
स भरद्वाजेन ससलिलेन पाणिनोरसि ताडितः सलक्षणोरस्कः संवृत्तः ॥

meaning.en: Long ago the sage Bharadvaja, coming to the heavenly Ganga to sprinkle himself, was approached by Vishnu taking his three strides. Bharadvaja struck him on the chest with a hand full of water, and his chest became marked with the sign.

verses.text: भृगुणा महर्षिणा शप्तोऽग्निः सर्वभक्षत्वमुपनीतः ॥

meaning.en: Cursed by the sage Bhrigu, Agni was made an eater of everything.

verses.text:
अदितिर्वै देवानामन्नमपचदेतद्भुक्त्वासुरान्हनिष्यन्तीति ।
तत्र बुधो व्रतचर्यासमाप्तावागच्छत् ।
अदितिं चावोचद्भिक्षां देहीति ।
तत्र देवैः पूर्वमेतत्प्राश्यं नान्येनेत्यदितिर्भिक्षां नादात् ।
अथ भिक्षाप्रत्याख्यानरुषितेन बुधेन ब्रह्मभूतेन विवस्वतो द्वितीये जन्मन्यण्डसंज्ञितस्याण्डं मारितमदित्याः ।
स मार्तण्डो विवस्वानभवच्छ्राद्धदेवः ॥

meaning.en: Aditi once cooked food for the gods, so that eating it they would slay the asuras. Budha came there at the end of his vow, and said to Aditi, "Give me alms." Aditi, thinking "The gods must eat this first, no one else," did not give. Budha, angered at the refusal and having become Brahman, killed the egg of Aditi's "egg-named" son, in Vivasvan's second birth. He became Martanda Vivasvan, Shraddhadeva.

verses.text:
दक्षस्य वै दुहितरः षष्टिरासन् ।
ताभ्यः कश्यपाय त्रयोदश प्रादाद्दश धर्माय दश मनवे सप्तविंशतिमिन्दवे ।
तासु तुल्यासु नक्षत्राख्यां गतासु सोमो रोहिण्यामभ्यधिकां प्रीतिमकरोत् ।
ततस्ताः शेषाः पत्न्य ईर्ष्यावत्यः पितुः समीपं गत्वेममर्थं शशंसुः ।
भगवन्नस्मासु तुल्यप्रभावासु सोमो रोहिणीमधिकं भजतीति ।
सोऽब्रवीद्यक्ष्मैनमावेक्ष्यतीति ॥

meaning.en: Daksha had sixty daughters. He gave thirteen to Kashyapa, ten to Dharma, ten to Manu, and twenty-seven to Soma. Though they were equal and became the stars, Soma showed greater love for Rohini. Then the other wives, jealous, went to their father and told him: "Blessed one, though we are equal in rank, Soma favors Rohini more." He said, "Consumption will seize him."

verses.text:
दक्षशापात्सोमं राजानं यक्ष्माविवेश ।
स यक्ष्मणाविष्टो दक्षमगमत् ।
दक्षश्चैनमब्रवीन्न समं वर्तस इति ।
तत्रर्षयः सोममब्रुवन्क्षीयसे यक्ष्मणा ।
पश्चिमस्यां दिशि समुद्रे हिरण्यसरस्तीर्थम् ।
तत्र गत्वात्मानमभिषेचयस्वेति ।
अथागच्छत्सोमस्तत्र हिरण्यसरस्तीर्थम् ।
गत्वा चात्मनः स्नपनमकरोत् ।
स्नात्वा चात्मानं पाप्मनो मोक्षयामास ।
तत्र चावभासितस्तीर्थे यदा सोमस्तदाप्रभृति तीर्थं तत्प्रभासमिति नाम्ना ख्यातं बभूव ।
तच्छापादद्यापि क्षीयते सोमोऽमावास्यान्तरस्थः ।
पौर्णमासीमात्रेऽधिष्ठितो मेघलेखाप्रतिच्छन्नं वपुर्दर्शयति ।
मेघसदृशं वर्णमगमत्तदस्य शशलक्ष्म विमलमभवत् ॥

meaning.en: By Daksha's curse, consumption entered King Soma. Afflicted, he went to Daksha, who said, "You are not treating them equally." The sages said to Soma, "You are wasting with consumption. In the western direction, in the ocean, is the Hiranyasaras tirtha. Go there and bathe." Soma went to Hiranyasaras tirtha and bathed, and freed himself of the sin. Because Soma shone at that tirtha, it became known as Prabhasa. Through that curse the moon still wanes, between new moons; at full moon he shows his body veiled by a streak of cloud, took on a cloud-like hue, and his hare mark became bright.

verses.text:
स्थूलशिरा महर्षिर्मेरोः प्रागुत्तरे दिग्भागे तपस्तेपे ।
तस्य तपस्तप्यमानस्य सर्वगन्धवहः शुचिर्वायुर्विवायमानः शरीरमस्पृशत् ।
स तपसा तापितशरीरः कृशो वायुनोपवीज्यमानो हृदयपरितोषमगमत् ।
तत्र तस्यानिलव्यजनकृतपरितोषस्य सद्यो वनस्पतयः पुष्पशोभां न दर्शितवन्त इति स एताञ्शशाप न सर्वकालं पुष्पवन्तो भविष्यथेति ॥

meaning.en: The great sage Sthulashiras practiced austerity in the north-east of Meru. As he did, a pure wind carrying all fragrances blew and touched his body. His body scorched by austerity and gaunt, fanned by the wind, he felt heart's delight. Because the trees did not at once show the beauty of flowers for him, so pleased by the wind's fanning, he cursed them: "You shall not bear flowers at all times."

verses.text:
नारायणो लोकहितार्थं वडवामुखो नाम महर्षिः पुराभवत् ।
तस्य मेरौ तपस्तप्यतः समुद्र आहूतो नागतः ।
तेनामर्षितेनात्मगात्रोष्मणा समुद्रः स्तिमितजलः कृतः ।
स्वेदप्रस्यन्दनसदृशश्चास्य लवणभावो जनितः ।
उक्तश्चापेयो भविष्यसि ।
एतच्च ते तोयं वडवामुखसंज्ञितेन पीयमानं मधुरं भविष्यति ।
तदेतदद्यापि वडवामुखसंज्ञितेनानुवर्तिना तोयं सामुद्रं पीयते ॥

meaning.en: For the welfare of the worlds, Narayana long ago became the great sage named Vadavamukha. As he practiced austerity on Meru, he summoned the ocean, which did not come. Angered, with the heat of his body he made the ocean's waters still, and made them salty like drops of sweat, and said: "You will be undrinkable. Only when drunk by one called Vadavamukha will your water be sweet." So even now, by a follower named Vadavamukha, the ocean's water is drunk.

verses.text:
हिमवतो गिरेर्दुहितरमुमां रुद्रश्चकमे ।
भृगुरपि च महर्षिर्हिमवन्तमागम्याब्रवीत्कन्यामुमां मे देहीति ।
तमब्रवीद्धिमवानभिलषितो वरो रुद्र इति ।
तमब्रवीद्भृगुर्यस्मात्त्वयाहं कन्यावरणकृतभावः प्रत्याख्यातस्तस्मान्न रत्नानां भवान्भाजनं भविष्यतीति ।
अद्यप्रभृत्येतदवस्थितमृषिवचनम् ॥

meaning.en: Rudra desired Uma, daughter of the Himalaya. The great sage Bhrigu also came to Himalaya and said, "Give me your daughter Uma." Himalaya said, "Rudra is the husband I desire." Bhrigu told him, "Since I, who came with the intent of asking for your daughter, was refused, you will not be a vessel of jewels." From that day the sage's word has stood.

verses.text:
तदेवंविधं माहात्म्यं ब्राह्मणानाम् ।
क्षत्रमपि शाश्वतीमव्ययां पृथिवीं पत्नीमभिगम्य बुभुजे ।
तदेतद्ब्रह्माग्नीषोमीयम् ।
तेन जगद्धार्यते ॥

meaning.en: Such is the greatness of brahmins. The kshatriya too, taking the eternal, imperishable earth as wife, enjoyed her. This is the Brahma-Agni-Soma doctrine, by which the world is upheld.
